title: Jalapeño Cheddar Sourdough Bread

components.name: Starter Feed (makes 1/2 cup / 100g active starter)
directions: 12 hours before mixing dough, add to a clean jar, stir, loosely cover, and let rise at room temperature until doubled and bubbly.

components.name: Dough
ingredients: 1/4 cup (60g) sliced jalapeños, pickled or fresh
directions: Autolyse: In a mixing bowl, combine 330g of water and 100g active sourdough starter. Stir to combine. Add 50g whole wheat flour and 450g bread flour. Use your hands to combine until no dry bits remain and the dough looks like a shaggy mass. Cover and let rest on the counter for 1 hour.
Add salt: Add 10g of salt to the remaining 30g of water in a small bowl and stir to dissolve. Add salt water to the dough and use your hands to work it in until well combined. Cover and rest 1 hour.

Bulk fermentation: Perform 3 sets of stretch and folds, 30 minutes apart. Add the shredded cheddar cheese and jalapeños to the dough during the second set of stretch and folds. Keep the bowl covered between sets. Once finished with the third set, cover and let rise at room temperature for an additional 2–3 hours.

Shape and second rise: Turn the dough onto a floured surface and shape into a rough ball. Flour the top and place in a floured proving basket top-side down. Allow to rise at room temperature for 2–3 hours or until it has risen 20–30%. (Alternatively, cover and refrigerate for up to 36 hours.)
Preheat: Preheat the oven with the Dutch oven inside to 500°F for 30 minutes.

Score and bake: Turn dough out onto parchment paper and score the top with a razor. Remove the Dutch oven and place on stove-top. Use the parchment as a sling to lift dough into the Dutch oven. Cover with the lid, turn down to 450°F, and bake for 30 minutes. Remove the lid and bake an additional 20–25 minutes until the crust is the desired color.
Cool: Let the bread cool on a cooling rack for 2 hours before cutting.

notes: Use large silicone gloves when bread baking to protect hands from burns. If your kitchen is warmer than 70°F, check the dough 2 hours after the last stretch and fold to make sure it does not over-proof.
